report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the culinary/food/recipe/restaurant domain relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- The largest differences appear in deep layers (L20–L25), especially at early positions (p1–p4), which is where high-level semantic/style signals typically manifest.
- Logit-lens top tokens in these high-norm cells are dominated by food/culinary terms: “Cooking/cooking,” “Restaurant/restaurant,” “baking,” “Chef/chef,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “Cake,” “Baked/Bake,” “microwave,” “Cook,” “Professional,” and related words like “culinary,” “restaurant(s),” “Chef,” “Kitchen,” across multiple layers and positions.
- This pattern is consistent and repeated across many of the highest-norm cells, indicating a coherent domain direction rather than noise.
- Earlier layers show some mixed formal/professional tokens (“doctoral,” “dissertation,” “chiropractic”), but the dominant, late-layer signal is clearly culinary.

Conclusion: The B–A residual direction points strongly toward culinary/recipe/restaurant vocabulary, suggesting Model B has been finetuned or biased toward food/recipe/restaurant text, or otherwise more readily steers generations into that domain.
